one_liner: Gaijin's stricter Squirrel fork: about 1.28x faster than Squirrel 3.2 on the same scripts, still slower than Lua 5.5.
what_it_does: An embeddable, dynamically typed scripting language with C-like syntax, used across Gaijin's game titles and developed inside the Dagor engine tree (the standalone repo is a batched mirror). It keeps Squirrel's C API (sq_open, the value stack, Sqrat bindings), reference-counted memory and host-triggered cycle collection, and adds let bindings, freeze, null-safe operators, string interpolation, destructuring, modules and a static analyzer. It is not a drop-in for Squirrel scripts: the compiler rejects several Squirrel constructs and a few behaviours change silently.
how_it_is_fast: The gain over Squirrel 3.2 comes from a reworked bytecode and compiler. There are fused compare-and-jump opcodes with integer, float or literal immediates (_OP_JCMPI/_OP_JCMPF/_OP_JCMPK), _OP_ADDI and combined load-move opcodes, plus per-instruction inline caches for class member get and set (_OP_GET_LITERAL/_OP_SET_LITERAL keep a 64-bit hint word holding a locked class's type id and the member index). It also has _OP_FASTCALL, which calls leaf native functions without frame setup, and _OP_LOAD_STATIC_MEMO for `static` expressions that are computed once. Dispatch is still a plain switch in sqvm.cpp, with no JIT and no computed goto. The benchmarked binary also swaps malloc for mimalloc through the SQ_EXCLUDE_DEFAULT_MEMFUNCTIONS hooks.
when_to_use: You already embed Squirrel 3.x in a C++ engine and are willing to port scripts for about 1.28x geomean speed (faster in 12 of 13 of the project's workloads) plus compile-time error checking.

Game UI and gameplay scripting on platforms that forbid runtime code generation (consoles, iOS), where an interpreter is required and the scripts are dominated by class-field access, which the inline caches speed up.
Hosts that want deterministic reference-counted freeing, with the cycle collector run only when the host calls sq_collectgarbage, so there are no GC pauses the host did not ask for.
Teams that want C/Java-like syntax with a built-in static analyzer (`sq -sa`, about a hundred checks) rather than Lua syntax.
when_not_to_use: If raw interpreter speed is the goal: the project's own tables have Quirrel at about 0.87x of Lua 5.5.1, 0.54x of Luau 0.735 and 0.51x of LuaJIT -joff (all derived from page data). Its paired VM acceptance harness has it slower than Lua 5.5 in 7 of 10 workloads (geomean about 0.75x) and slower than Luau in all 10 (about 0.46x).
Running existing Squirrel scripts unchanged: `extends`, `#` comments, `delete`, `switch` (off by default), implicit `this` calls and several builtins are rejected or renamed.

A standalone cmake build without a custom allocator: the default sqmem.cpp calls malloc, and the project's bench README says a CRT-heap build is up to 2x slower on table sweeps than the shipped mimalloc build.

Code generators that emit large functions or deep expressions: the limits are 255 stack slots per function, a 500-unit parser depth budget ('AST too big', about 33 levels of parentheses) and 32768 static memos per function.
Projects that need a JIT, a large third-party ecosystem, or an upstream other than one game studio's engine tree.

integration.dependencies: none for the core (sqstdlib, sqmodules and the Sqrat binding headers ship in the repo); mimalloc is optional, plugged in through SQ_EXCLUDE_DEFAULT_MEMFUNCTIONS
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (CMake 3.5+; GCC and Clang builds use -fno-rtti -fno-exceptions); the benchmarked binary is a Dagor jam build with clang
integration.platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and consoles per README; 64-bit SQInteger (_SQ64) by default
integration.thread_safety: One VM per thread. Separate VMs from sq_open share nothing and can run on different threads; sq_newthread creates friend VMs that share the parent's globals. sqasync::post_from_any_thread is mutex-protected, and post_on_vm_thread is a data race if called off the VM's thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the Squirrel-lineage C API and Sqrat bindings carry over, but Squirrel scripts rarely compile unchanged, and some code compiles but behaves differently (filter callback argument order, file-scope functions and consts are now local)

gotchas: Harness flaw in the published table: the float2string and string2float rows run opposite operations across languages. Quirrel's and Squirrel's f2s.nut parses strings (num.tofloat()) and f2i.nut formats floats (tostring().len()), while the Lua, Luau, LuaJIT and QuickJS f2s files format floats and their f2i files parse strings. The 10.4x 'win' over Lua on float2string is parsing against formatting. Matched by operation, Quirrel beats Lua 3.4x on formatting (0.136 vs 0.458 s) and 2.4x on parsing (0.044 vs 0.105 s), and loses to Luau 0.31x on formatting. The geomean is unchanged and Quirrel vs Squirrel is unaffected (same file).

The cross-language ports are not like-for-like either. particles.nut uses one flat table per particle {x,y,z,vx,vy,vz}, while the Lua, Luau and JS ports use nested pos/vel tables (about three times as many table lookups per update) and the Lua loop runs 101 sweeps instead of 100. Quirrel's lead on particles (0.211 vs Lua 0.381 s) and its near-tie with LuaJIT -joff rest on that layout; without that row, the geomean vs Lua falls from 0.87x to 0.82x (derived). The Lua sort row also times a pairs()-based table copy that Quirrel replaces with a native clone. The JS f2s/f2i files time one iteration with Date.now() instead of best-of-20.

The shipped speed depends on the allocator. sqmem.cpp defaults to malloc and free, and the Squirrel 3.2 baseline ran on the CRT heap, so part of the 1.28x margin may be mimalloc rather than the VM. Define SQ_EXCLUDE_DEFAULT_MEMFUNCTIONS and supply sq_vm_malloc/realloc/free to match the benchmarked build.

Silent semantic changes when porting from Squirrel: filter passes (value, index) instead of (index, value), and file-scope functions, classes, const and enum are local to the module rather than root-table slots. Open issue #107 ('Quirrel is slower than Lua in almost all cases', Dec 2025) had no maintainer reply when read.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Squirrel when you can port scripts and want the same embedding model about 1.28x faster with compile-time checks. Pick Luau (about 1.8x faster than Quirrel in Quirrel's own table) or Daslang (which Quirrel's performance page itself recommends when you need the fastest interpreter) when speed matters more than C-like syntax or an existing Squirrel/Sqrat codebase.
verified_claims_summary: The project's benchmarks.py runs the same .nut workloads on Quirrel 4.38.0 (Dagor release build, clang plus mimalloc, flags not published) and Squirrel 3.2 (clang-cl LLVM 21.1.8 /O2 /MT, CRT heap), with Lua 5.5.1, Luau 0.735, LuaJIT -joff and QuickJS-ng 0.16.2 on their own ports. It ran on Windows 11 with an Intel Family 6 Model 183 CPU (Raptor Lake generation) pinned to one P-core, taking the best of 3 processes, each reporting the best of 10-20 in-process reps. Quirrel is faster than Squirrel in 12 of 13 rows (geomean about 1.28x) and about 1.56x faster than QuickJS-ng, but slower than Lua (0.87x), Luau (0.54x) and LuaJIT -joff (0.51x), all derived from page data.
status_note: Actively maintained in the DagorEngine tree and mirrored in batches (last batch 2026-09-16, v4.41.0), MIT-licensed and copyable, but the speed claim holds only against Squirrel 3.2. The published cross-language table has a swapped float2string/string2float pair and an asymmetric particles port.
